description: Trigonometric parallaxes and proper motions of ~200 masers in high-mass star-forming regions measured by VLBI (BeSSeL/VLBA, VERA, EVN, LBA). These are the direct observational constraints on the spiral structure in arms.json.

source.paper: Reid M.J., Menten K.M., Brunthaler A., et al. 2019, ApJ, 885, 131
source.title: Trigonometric Parallaxes of High-mass Star-forming Regions: Our View of the Milky Way
source.version: VizieR catalogue J/ApJ/885/131, prepared by CDS 16-Sep-2021 (199 rows)

licence: Table reproduced from an AAS journal article (ApJ) via VizieR/CDS. Cite Reid et al. 2019, ApJ 885, 131 and the VizieR service. See LICENSE.md in this directory.
attribution: Maser parallaxes: Reid et al. (2019), ApJ 885, 131 — VizieR J/ApJ/885/131 (CDS, Strasbourg).

frame.galactic: IAU galactic (l, b in degrees); NGP alpha=192.85948, delta=27.12825, l_NCP=122.93192
frame.cartesian: Galactocentric: origin at the Galactic centre, +X along galactic rotation at the Sun (toward l=90deg), +Y from the Galactic centre toward the Sun, +Z toward the NGP. Sun at (0, 8.15, 0.0055) kpc. beta = atan2(X, Y), the Reid+2019 galactocentric azimuth (0 toward the Sun, increasing with galactic rotation).

epoch: J2000.0 positions; proper motions as published (observation epochs 2003-2019)
recordNote: armName is not stored per record: resolve armCode against the top-level armCodes map. armFit names the arms.json arm this source constrains, or null when Table 2 has no fit for it.
notes: Distances are the naive parallax inverse 1/plx. Reid+2019 themselves recommend a Bayesian distance estimator for individual sources; for a 3D atlas the inverse is adequate, and the asymmetric bounds 1/(plx+e_plx) and 1/(plx-e_plx) follow directly from plxMas/ePlxMas.
Parallax uncertainties for sources with multiple (N) maser spots were adjusted upwards by sqrt(N) by the authors (ReadMe note 1).
Galactic (l, b) are computed here from the catalogue J2000 RA/Dec; they agree with the galactic coordinates encoded in each source name to better than 0.020 deg over 199 checked sources.
